The Caliph, however, under compulsion,
and unwillingly, wrote and praised his diligence and his zeal on behalf of the faith,
and urged him not to delay his coming to Baghdad.
But the army of the Daylamites and the Turks who were in Baghdad and their leaders rebelled and said:
'This cannot be, that the Ghuzz should come to Baghdad.
And if they come,
we are prepared for war.'
And when their petition profited them nothing,
after a few days the forces of the Ghuzz burst forth
and reached the territory of Baghdad.
Then the chief of chiefs, the chief judge, and many of the nobles of Baghdad went out to meet the Sultan,
and approached him where he had encamped.
And they spoke with him admonitory words on behalf of the Caliph,
that he should not give leave to his forces to lay waste the land of Baghdad,
because it is the seat of the Caliphate,
and in it stands the law of the faith.
And the Sultan received their words with goodwill,
and assented to their counsel.
And when he approached and encamped at the gate called that of the Deaconess,
the Daylamites, the Turks, and some of the common people of Baghdad rioted,
and drew swords against the Ghuzz who were entering the city to buy provisions for themselves,
and straw and fodder for their horses.
Then the emirs of the Ghuzz mounted and entered Baghdad,
and killed a great number of the Daylamites, Turks, and common people.
And they seized their leaders,
and brought them to the Sultan.
And he commanded,
and they were imprisoned near him in tents, bound in fetters.
And the Sultan sent to the Caliph,
and complained about the riot which the people of Baghdad had caused.
And he made known:
'Certain of the Daylamites of his service were found killed,
and others were not found at all.
And were it not for your honor,
the whole of Baghdad would have been destroyed by the edge of the sword.'
And when the Caliph had been comforted by such words and fear had departed from his heart,
he sent gifts with his eunuchs and nobles to the Sultan.
And as soon as they came near the camp,
the Sultan commanded, and they were all bound in fetters,
and everything that was with them was plundered.
